title: Introduction
text: In this tutorial, you will build a full-stack React app using FormCMS and Cursor — without writing a single line of backend code.

title: Step 1: Start Backend
text: Step 1: Start the FormCMS backend. Run this Docker command in your terminal. It exposes port 5000 for the REST API, the admin portal, and the built-in MCP server.

title: Step 1: Admin Setup
text: Open localhost 5000 slash mate. Follow the setup wizard to create your super admin account.

title: Step 1: API Key
text: Next, go to Settings, then API Key Configuration, and click Generate. Copy this key — you will need it in the next step.

title: Step 2: MCP Config
text: Step 2: Connect Cursor to FormCMS. In your project root, create the file dot cursor slash mcp dot json. Add the FormCMS MCP server entry with its SSE URL and an Authorization header. Paste your API key as the Bearer token value.

title: Step 3: AI Skill
text: Step 3: Add the AI rules file. Run this curl command to download the FormCMS skill into dot cursor slash rules. This teaches Cursor how to use FormCMS APIs — schema design, data seeding, and deployment.

title: Step 4: Scaffold
text: Step 4: Scaffold the project. Open the Cursor chat panel and type this prompt. Cursor will create a Vite plus React app, configure the proxy, define your schema entities, seed sample data, and start the dev server — all automatically.

title: Step 5: Frontend
text: Step 5: Build the frontend. Ask Cursor to build components like PostList and PostDetail. Because Cursor already knows your schema from the MCP tools, it uses the correct field names automatically.

title: Step 6: Deploy
text: Step 6: Deploy. Tell Cursor to build and deploy as the home page. It runs npm run build, zips the output, and calls the deploy SPA MCP tool. Your full-stack app is now live from a single container.

title: Conclusion
text: That is it. You now have a full-stack React application — schema, data, frontend, and deployment — built entirely through Cursor. No manual backend work required.
